page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine belonging to the compute-optimized C2D family, provisioned with a memory-skewed resource profile. It is equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 processor cores with 2 threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local ephemeral storage, requiring attached persistent disks for non-volatile storage needs.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded performance offset by modest aggregate multi-threaded capacity due to the 4-vCPU limit. In stress-ng testing, single-core execution reached 2922.28, placing in the top quartile, whereas multi-core throughput of 5861.67 landed in the lower quartile. Geekbench tests follow this pattern, registering 1652.0 in single-core and 3741.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory throughput tests show uncached sequential read speeds of 46.82 GB/sec and write speeds of 27.55 GB/sec. Data processing benchmarks reflect standard mid-tier performance, such as 28.24 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 12.0 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside a PassMark memory score of 2528.93.

The primary tradeoff of the c2d-highmem-4 lies in its combination of high per-core single-thread speed and memory density against constrained parallel processing capability. Tasks reliant on heavy concurrency, such as large database operations (1878.57 PassMark rating) or high-volume multi-core compilation (4222.0 in Clang tests), are bounded by the 4-vCPU ceiling. Qualitatively, the instance offers cost-efficient utility for memory-heavy services that do not justify high core counts, such as mid-sized in-memory caches, memory-bound worker processes, moderate text-generation inference pipelines, and light transactional databases.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-4 is a memory-focused instance configuration within the compute-optimized C2D series, driven by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 32.0 GB of memory, equating to 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server lacks local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates robust single-core throughput, recording 2922.28 in stress-ng single-core tests, balanced by moderate aggregate multi-core output. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 46.82 GB/sec for reads and 27.55 GB/sec for writes. The c2d-highmem-4 provides an efficient resource footprint for memory-demanding applications requiring capable single-threaded CPU speed, such as distributed memory caching, light database servers, background job processing, and small-model inference tasks.
